commit_reviews.summary: Clean greenfield scaffolding that wires a standard ts-jest Node test setup with committed lockfile, matching the project's TypeScript SSG stack.

problems: template path coupling asserted via magic strings
commit_reviews.summary: Adds well-structured template-rendering tests that extend the existing setup pattern with a `setupTemplateDir` helper, covering default/custom/fallback layouts, partials, and template data.

problems: lockfile-only diff means source usage can't be verified
single commit bundles three distinct feature dependencies
commit_reviews.summary: Session 3 integration adds the canonical dependency set for an SSG (chokidar for watch mode, handlebars for templating, ws for live-reload) with a clean, npm-generated lockfile that correctly re-flags now-runtime deps out of devDependencies and includes matching @types/ws.

compounding_issues: Story aborted after 3 of 5 sessions due to a 900s timeout on session 3, so the planned refactor and cross_cutting sessions never ran and the story ends mid-sequence

The mismatched bad_seed Auth API (index.ts, 200 lines) was never integrated or removed; it remains orphaned dead code at the tip with dependencies (express, jwt, sqlite3, bcryptjs) absent from package.json

node_modules (5394 files) and dist/ (322 files) are committed into git with no .gitignore, bloating every commit and making session diffs dominated by dependency noise (session 2's visible diff was mostly compiled output)
Session 2's template engine kept the session 1 inline-HTML generator as a fallback path, creating two parallel rendering implementations that must be kept in sync
Frontend HTML generation is duplicated across generatePageHtml/generateIndexHtml and the new pageBodyHtml/indexBodyHtml template helpers rather than unified
key_decisions: Session 1 ignored the mismatched seed and performed a greenfield rewrite of the SSG using commander CLI + gray-matter frontmatter + markdown-it, rather than salvaging the Auth API seed
Session 2 adopted Handlebars for layouts/partials with a TemplateEngine class and template support in frontmatter, while retaining the hardcoded HTML path as a fallback
Session 3 added a live-reload dev server (chokidar file watching + WebSocket via ws, debounced rebuilds) and integrated the serve command into the existing CLI
Committing compiled dist/ artifacts and full node_modules into the repo, coupling generated output to source history
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across the three completed sessions: session 1 produced a functional but primitive single-file generator with hardcoded inline HTML, session 2 introduced a proper Handlebars layout/partial engine with template selection in frontmatter and a substantial test suite, and session 3 integrated a production-grade dev server with chokidar watching and WebSocket live-reload wired cleanly into the CLI (reviewer architectural-fit scores 0.9 to 0.88, all exits clean). The arc is a textbook greenfield-to-feature-to-integration progression, but it accumulated technical debt along the way — orphaned seed code, committed node_modules and dist bloat, duplicated rendering paths, and magic-string template coupling — and the run never reached its planned refactor and cross-cutting sessions, so long-term cleanliness was never verified.
story_review.summary: A coherent and genuinely progressive three-session build of a static site generator that improved steadily in capability and integration, but was truncated by a timeout before its refactor phase and left behind significant hygiene debt (orphaned seed code, committed dependencies, duplicated rendering logic).
